chapter: Gulf Coast bands and early jobs
title: First New Orleans job at the Silver Slipper and return to Spring Hill
summary: First piano job in New Orleans at the Silver Slipper during Prohibition in 1926; Brunies band, then back to Spring Hill and LSU.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Oh, yes it was. Then? Yes. As far as... If anyone was ever caught, I don't know of anybody ever going to jail with it on account of it. But all you had to do was go down to St. Philip Street and knock on the wall and stick your finger in the hole for the... and 20 cents was all you could afford in those days. So it was... The first piano job that I had when I left Mobile and came to New Orleans was at the Silver Slipper and that was with a little small push-around piano, short keyboard about that big and I played... It was during Prohibition and I played for girls singers to go around to push around tables during intermission. Merritt Brunis had the band there. Henry Brunis played trombone in the band. Bullfellow played piano from Biloxi.

Buck Rogers played drums. Red, I can't remember his last name from Biloxi, played sax. Not Parks Wilkes now, Parks Wilkes played over on the Gulf Coast with Ellis Stratikas. That was where I first knew Ellis Stratikas was on the coast. That was before Ellis Stratikas came to New Orleans to play.
When did you come to New Orleans first?
1926, then I left and went back to school.
And when did you go to Spring Hill?
Went on back to Spring Hill almost. I was only here in New Orleans just a year, then I went to Spring Hill.
27. And then you went on to LSU?
